nodes.value: Table VII reports completion rate, task duration, slip count, damage count and CPUT for each method across five contact-rich tasks. High slip counts indicate poor force and slippage feedback. ALOHA records up to 27 slips (USB plug) and 14 damages (Fragile cup), reflecting its indirect force perception. UMI improves the force feedback and records zero damage events, yet its multilink transmission still permits noticeable slippage in forcesensitive tasks (e.g., 26 slips during Stamp press). In contrast, FreeTacMan limits slips to at most 2 and records zero damage across all tasks, evidencing its high-fidelity, low-latency tactile feedback. As a combined metric of efficiency and reliability, CPUT highlights the overall advantage of FreeTacMan: it achieves scores from 0.2292 (USB plug) to 0.33

contexts: Recently, handheld interfaces like Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) Chi et al. [2024] ; Liu et al. [2025b] ; 【Zhaxizhuoma et al. [2025]】 have emerged as a pivotal medium between humans and robots. These UMI systems bridge the embodiment gap by having operators guide a gripper mechanically identical to the robot's end-effector.

[2024] introduced a portable pistol-grip device to collect demonstrations at a low cost. Subsequent UMI-style systems improve collection scale and throughput Liu et al. [2025b] ; 【Zhaxizhuoma et al. [2025]】 ; Lin et al. [2024] , add tactile sensing for contact-rich manipulation Liu et al. [2025a] ; Li et al. [2025] ; Liang et al. [2025] ; Xu et al.

Our dataset is significantly larger than previous UMI-based datasets, such as the Fast-UMI data (≈ 60 hours and 22 tasks) 【Zhaxizhuoma et al. [2025]】 and the original UMI data (12 hours and 4 tasks) Chi et al. [2024] .
The conventional pistol-grip interface introduces a mechanical offset between the operator's fingers and the gripper's pinch-point, significantly reducing haptic transparency 【Wu et al. [2026]】 .
